criterion_notes.T2: Ten works, each with title, year, medium, dimensions and a price in euro, from €1,800 to €5,200.
criterion_notes.T3: Every work opens its own view with medium, dimensions, price and a paragraph on how the piece was painted.
criterion_notes.T4: Adding a work, pressing 'Proceed to checkout', filling name, email, address, city and country and placing the order returns reference MH-VKJU-5OZ0 with a dated confirmation. The order itself lives only in the browser: there is no orders table in the project database, and a reload loses the confirmation.
criterion_notes.T6: The message appears as one row in the project's contact_messages table — checked in Bolt's database view, not just in the confirmation text.

notes: One prompt, one run of the plan, 32 minutes, 8 of 8 — and the first run in this set where the storefront half and the admin half both work in the same build. Bolt wrote a real database table and wired the contact form to it: the message shows up as a row in contact_messages, which is the check that most builders fail. The catalogue is the strongest content in any Bolt run (ten works, dimensions, a paragraph per painting, curated-looking picsum images), and the cart, checkout and reference number all hold. Two honest limits: the order is not stored anywhere server-side, so the confirmation disappears on reload although the brief asked for it to survive; and the site is a client-side app, so all ten works live behind /#/ and only the home page is visible to a crawler. No horizontal scroll at 320, 390 or 430 px, no console errors; axe finds contrast on the small caps labels.
